post.caption:
Newcomen's engine heated a cylinder full of steam and then cooled the same cylinder to collapse it, throwing away the previous stroke's heat every single time. Watt's separate condenser moved the cooling next door so the cylinder stayed hot, cutting fuel use dramatically. That is what turned a mine pump into factory power, then ships and trains. One modern car engine sustains the work of several hundred horses, and that multiplier applied to every task is the Industrial Revolution.
